content.value_statement: Azure Event Hubs and Service Bus failures can be difficult to isolate across SDK, configuration, and service layers. This skill guides focused checks using Azure resources, diagnostic logs, and current Microsoft Learn guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides diagnosis of Azure Event Hubs and Service Bus SDK connection failures.
Covers authentication, AMQP link, timeout, reconnection, and receiver issues.
Checks namespace health and lists messaging entities through Azure MCP tools.
Queries Azure diagnostic logs with KQL through the monitoring MCP tool.
Reviews retry, prefetch, batch size, entity, consumer group, and checkpoint settings.
Searches Microsoft Learn and cites relevant troubleshooting guidance.
limitations: Requires configured Azure MCP tools and sufficient Azure permissions for live resource checks.
Does not include the detailed messaging guides stored in the separate azure-diagnostics skill.
Does not change Azure resources or application code through the documented workflow.
Focuses on Azure Event Hubs and Service Bus SDK issues, not all Azure messaging products.

use_cases.title: Resolve SDK exceptions
use_cases.description: Identify likely causes and focused checks for connection, authentication, AMQP, timeout, and lock errors.

use_cases.title: Investigate processing incidents
use_cases.description: Correlate service health, diagnostic logs, and SDK configuration when receivers or event processors stop handling messages.

use_cases.title: Support Azure messaging users
use_cases.description: Review resource topology, configuration details, and current Microsoft guidance before recommending remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Identify an SDK error
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Azure messaging error: [error]. The service is [Event Hubs or Service Bus], and the SDK language is [language].
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a known error and basic environment details.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate connection failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate repeated [timeout, disconnect, or AMQP error] for [namespace and entity]. Check resource health, configuration, and current Microsoft Learn guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Trace recurring connection failures across service and client settings.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze message processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze why [processor or receiver] stops handling messages. Review locks, sessions, retries, prefetch, batch size, checkpoints, and relevant diagnostic logs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Examine a complex receiver or processor reliability issue.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate production failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a diagnosis for [incident]. Correlate SDK version, timestamps, KQL log evidence, resource health, configuration, and documented remediation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an evidence-based diagnosis for a recurring production incident.

output_examples.input: Our Service Bus receiver reports MessageLockLost during batch processing.
output: Likely cause: processing exceeds the message lock duration or lock renewal fails.
Check processing time, lock duration, renewal settings, prefetch, and batch size.
Review diagnostic logs around the failure timestamp before changing configuration.

output_examples.input: An Event Hubs processor receives duplicate events after restarting.
output: Verify the consumer group, checkpoint store, checkpoint frequency, and restart behavior.
Duplicates can occur when processing completes before the latest checkpoint is persisted.
Confirm that downstream processing is idempotent.

output_examples.input: The Java client repeatedly disconnects with an AMQP link detach error.
output: Check Azure resource health and collect the full detach condition and timestamp.
Review network idle timeouts, SDK version, retry settings, and diagnostic logs.
Compare the evidence with current Microsoft Learn guidance for that detach condition.

best_practices: Provide the service, SDK language, SDK version, full error message, and approximate failure time.
Grant Azure MCP tools only the permissions needed to inspect the relevant subscription and namespace.
Validate proposed changes in a nonproduction environment and cite current Microsoft Learn guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not share connection strings, access keys, tokens, or message payloads in prompts.
Do not change retry, prefetch, or batch settings without measuring processing behavior.
Do not assume every SDK error is an Azure outage before checking application and network evidence.

faq.question: Which Azure services does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Event Hubs and Azure Service Bus SDK troubleshooting.

faq.question: Which SDK languages can it troubleshoot?
faq.answer: The workflow is language-neutral and can guide troubleshooting when you provide the SDK language, version, and error.

faq.question: Does it require access to my Azure subscription?
faq.answer: Live health, resource, and log checks require configured Azure MCP tools with appropriate permissions.

faq.question: Can it modify queues, topics, hubs, or application code?
faq.answer: The documented workflow performs diagnosis and recommends fixes. It does not describe resource or code changes.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the service, namespace, entity, SDK language, SDK version, error text, timestamps, and relevant configuration without secrets.

faq.question: Can it diagnose message lock and session lock errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers lock loss, lock expiration, renewal failures, session errors, prefetch, and batch processing behavior.
